how: The organizer proposes the mark and states an existing friends' plan, fitting the revised starter definition without requiring evidence of others joining.
The organizer explicitly invites participation beyond the friends whose plan is already stated.
The organizer proposes IOI letters in magenta beside SNSD, specifying the intended mark and relative location.
The organizer reports that the effort is almost done, establishing progress without claiming completion.
The organizer apologizes to the competing group while defending the need to take the spot quickly.
The warning identifies a competing attempt at the chosen spot, and the organizer justifies proceeding quickly before others take it.
The starter's invitation elaborates the same author's opening proposal, supporting a proposal followed by a call without proving that anyone joined.
An apology can acknowledge another group's claim while defending rapid occupation, without promising to yield, stop, or repair.
Anticipated loss of the opportunity to other placers supplies the organizer's stated reason for speed despite a competing claim.
The plan supplies a colour and relative location but no coded template or numeric coordinate.
Near completion does not establish upkeep or keepers repairing away an agreed design change.
The warning identifies another group's attempt rather than tracing who altered the proposed mark.
The warning and apology do not establish direct negotiations or agreed terms.
Competing attempts and an apology do not determine whether existing pixels were erased or encroached upon.
The plan names one location and the update reports progress without establishing loss or relocation.
Almost done reports progress rather than announcing or celebrating a finished mark.
The coded update does not establish recording the completed work or its fate.
The progress report contains no decision about retaining or continuing the effort.
The progress report leaves the means of placing unspecified and cannot establish machine assistance.
The starter's own update does not establish another participant's bare acceptance of the invitation.
Mentioning the competing community does not establish an exchange of help.
Placement in the K-pop corner establishes proximity without establishing coalition membership.
The qualified apology does not establish taunts, victory over a rival, or a continuing verbal contest.
The relative location and warning do not establish a host's authority over guest work.
The coded proposal and invitation do not establish containment of canvas talk or objections to it.
The warning and apology concern a spot without establishing a dispute or disclaimer about who may bind the community.
The coded progress report does not establish correction of an account or contest over preserved versions after placement ends.
The proposal and progress report do not establish an April Fools joke framing of the host room.
Anticipated competition does not establish a judgment that hands or room are insufficient.
The organizer explains speed through competition for the spot without identifying a prior quarrel.
Naming the fandom and choosing magenta do not establish imported lore, ideology, or devotion to a colour.
An existing friends' plan cannot establish that leadership, voting, sanctions, or division of work were never decided elsewhere.
The stated reason for speed does not identify a prior tie or rivalry as the reason for an attack.
Naming the competing community does not establish that the warning's author acts as its envoy.
The friends' plan is stated publicly without identifying a chat, its decisions, or a move into it.
Specifying a colour and relative location does not establish explanation of the canvas, its rules, or its controls.
The progress report does not establish visitors or returning members drawn into the room by the mark.
The plan and update do not establish new jokes made from the canvas work.
The invitation and friends' plan do not establish formation of a new room around a canvas mark.
The apology concerns taking a spot without establishing an argument over offensive words or hate symbols.
Representing a fandom in the mark does not establish seeking its creators' notice or receiving outside coverage.
The sad warning and qualified apology concern a competing claim without establishing an argument over whether covering art is fair.
The apology over a spot does not establish stress-driven withdrawal or repair of a personal quarrel.
The public plan and competing-spot warning do not establish concealing strategy or entering rival venues.
The proposal and progress report do not establish opposition to canvas posts producing attacks on the room's own mark.
The speed justification identifies competition for space without establishing constraints from sleep, work, travel, or devices.
The coded progress report does not establish site faults or technical fixes.
Concern about the competing group's attempt does not establish belonging to both communities.
An existing friends' plan precedes later progress, leaving whether the public invitation brought additional builders unresolved.
Near completion cannot establish the proposed transition from building into upkeep.
The competing-spot warning cannot establish upkeep producing border negotiations.
The qualified apology cannot establish a settled border producing restraint.
The progress report cannot establish upkeep strain leading to machine assistance.
Almost done leaves completion and ensuing celebration unestablished.
A progress update cannot establish celebration leading to preservation of the work.
The coded update cannot establish recording leading to continuation of the effort.
Anticipated competition does not establish insufficient hands causing relocation after loss.
The specified plan does not establish design discussion being settled by a template.
The invitation and starter's own update cannot establish another participant's bare acceptance or silent placing in response.
The warning and apology cannot establish upkeep strain prompting help between communities.
The warning and apology cannot establish border negotiations opening an exchange of help.
The invitation and competing claims leave an attack unestablished and cannot test recruitment turning into an attack call.
The warning and apology do not establish an attack call eliciting refusal, restraint, or apology.
Competing attempts do not establish an attack leading to a truce or deal.
The apology does not establish an attack producing a continuing verbal contest.
The location and competing claim cannot establish upkeep causing coalition membership.
The invitation cannot establish a resulting flood or a host response restricting canvas talk.
No agreement, disclaimer at its making, or later refusal of its binding force is established, leaving the revised bounded order untestable.
